svg.title: A simulated sampling distribution beside the density a flawed derivation claims
svg.desc: A histogram of twenty thousand simulated values of lambda hat peaks near 0.42 at a height close to 1.95, while the claimed density is a nearly flat curve peaking at 0.10, and its renormalized version peaks in the wrong place at 0.63.
svg.text: What the write-up claims, drawn to the scale of the data
twenty thousand samples of n = 5 from Exponential(rate 0.5)
its total area is 5 over 48, not one
the same shape rescaled to area one,
Simulated mean 0.6242 with a Monte Carlo standard error of 0.0026, against the claimed 0.5000.
That gap is about fifty Monte Carlo standard errors, so it is not sampling noise.
A curve that does not enclose unit area was never a density, whatever it was called.
